title: Rollback heuristics & commands scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad while chasing a canary rollback that showed different behavior between environments. Not for prime-time — raw commands, outputs, and hypotheses.

Summary of incident (short):
- Canary (us-west-2, pool-3) saw error surge during 2026-02-09 14:12–14:25 UTC.
- Traffic was ~12% of baseline, autoscaler stable, but ~40% of canary instances returned 500/502 spiky errors.
- Rollback triggered by canary-eject rule (latency+5xx) at 14:26. Services rolled back to build tag v2026.02.05-9c3a.
- Post-rollback: errors dropped to baseline but some clients observed model-response mismatch (embedding dims wrong) — suspicion: artifact tag mismatch in private registry cache.

Chronological breadcrumbs (what I ran, outputs I saw):

2026-02-09 14:30 UTC — initial checks
- kubectl get pods -n prod | grep canary
  Output: myservice-canary-7f8b9   1/1 Running   0  3m

- kubectl logs myservice-canary-7f8b9 -n prod --tail=200\  <-- saw bursts of stack traces with 'DecoderError: unexpected dim 1 != 768' and 'KVCacheMismatch: cache key not found'

Key error snippet (copied):
  2026-02-09T14:20:45Z ERROR model_inference.py:120 DecoderError: expected dim 768, got 256 at decode_tokens
  2026-02-09T14:20:45Z WARN cache_manager.py:78 KVCacheMismatch: cache miss for prefix 0x7b3f (attempting fallback)

Hypothesis A (artifact mismatch): the canary image pulled a variant model artifact (quantized vs float) causing shape mismatch and cache incompatibility. Could be tag collision or registry serving stale blob.

Quick checks performed:
- docker inspect registry.internal/redwood/myservice:v2026.02.09-canary | jq '.Config.Env'
  -> showed MODEL_TAG=v-emb-20260208-q4
- curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://registry.internal/v2/myservice/manifests/v2026.02.09-canary | jq '.layers[].digest'
  -> digests consistent with local staging images? Not matching staging manifest.

Command to fetch image digest on node (to compare):
- crictl inspecti $(crictl ps -a | grep myservice | awk '{print $1}') | jq '.info.imageRef'
  Note: on host found imageRef sha256:ab12cd... while registry manifest list had sha256:ff34ee... -> mismatch!

Hypothesis B (registry cache/proxy): private registry proxy (edge-cache) served an older blob when nodes pulled concurrently; some nodes got new digest, others old -> mixed cluster state -> KV cache keys incompatible across instances.

What I tried to validate B:
- curl -v https://registry-proxy.edge.internal/v2/myservice/blobs/sha256:ab12cd... 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'
  -> Returned 200 but headers showed "x-cache: HIT" on some requests and "x-cache: MISS" on others.
- Using httpie from two different k8s nodes produced different digests for the same blob URL (wtf).

Rollback mechanics I inspected:
- Helm release history: helm -n prod history myservice\  -> revision 124 -> bumped to 123 (rollback target) at 14:27 triggered via release controller.
- Controller logs indicated imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent for the canary, which would preserve old local images after rollback; but nodes had both old and new images - image reuse might have kept inconsistent runtime assets.

Local reproduction attempts (toy):
- Pulled both images locally on dev laptop and ran integration harness (simple HTTP load):
  docker pull registry.internal/redwood/myservice@sha256:ab12cd...
  docker run -e MODEL_TAG=v-emb-20260208-q4 ...
  Observed same DecoderError quickly when two local containers served concurrent requests and shared same Redis prefix for KV cache.

Quick mitigation steps I did during incident:
- Force-rolled nodes with canary pods to recreate with imagePullPolicy: Always by annotating deployment and cycling daemonset: kubectl -n prod set env deploy/myservice-canary FORCE_PULL=1
- Purged registry proxy cache for key prefixes: POST https://registry-proxy.edge.internal/admin/purge with body {"prefix":"/v2/myservice/"}
- Observed slow recovery; need to track if purge consistently returns 200 and proxies actually evict.

Post-incident validation checklist (to formalize later):
- [ ] Validate all nodes now reference the same image digest for the canary tag
- [ ] Ensure model artifacts inside image match expected MODEL_TAG env
- [ ] Confirm registry-proxy purge semantics: are blobs referenced by digest pinned elsewhere?
- [ ] Audit imagePullPolicy for release controller for canary flows (prefer Always for canaries)
- [ ] Add readiness gating: block traffic until both model version and kv-cache-format checksum match expected

Notes on artifact versioning policy (draft heuristics):
- Avoid using mutable tags for discovery during rollout (e.g., v2026.02.09-canary). Use digest-pin step in release controller when rolling out to avoid cross-node drift.
- On change to model artifact format (quantization/embedding-dim), include a migration window with two-format compatibility shim or zero-downtime migration steps and cache prefix rotation.

Commands and snippets I found helpful (copyable):
- Compare node imageRefs: kubectl get pods -n prod -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.containerStatuses[0].imageID}'\n' | sort -u
- Inspect registry manifest by digest: curl -H "Accept: application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json" https://registry.internal/v2/myservice/manifests/sha256:ab12cd...
- Check cache key prefixes in Redis (dev cluster): redis-cli -h redis-cache.internal KEYS 'kvcache:myservice:*' | wc -l

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- Does our registry-proxy invalidate blob digests on a tag update or only on TTL expiry? (I suspect TTL based). Ask infra to confirm TTL/pinning behavior.
- Should we change canary to use imagePullPolicy=Always? Tradeoff: slower start but prevents stale local images.
- Is there a safe way to rotate kv-cache prefixes atomically across rollout? Could use per-release prefix hashed from commit sha.

Lessons learned (quick):
- Mixed image digests across nodes are a real source of subtle runtime incompatibilities even when tags are identical.
- Image pull policy + registry caching + concurrency during rollout = recipe for mixed binaries.
- Canary health checks must validate both runtime binary version AND data format (e.g., model embedding dims, KV cache schema).

TODOs (next actions):
- [ ] Write short runbook entry for release-engineering playbook describing digest-pin best-practice. (Owner: me)
- [ ] Add e2e check in release pipeline: run small smoke test that decodes a dummy input and asserts embedding dim==768 before promoting canary traffic. (Owner: SRE)
- [ ] Add TTL/eviction test for registry-proxy in staging; coordinate with infra. (Owner: Lucas)
- [ ] Open follow-up Jira: JIRA-RELEASE-4128 "Ensure registry-proxy consistent blob retrieval during concurrent pulls"

Random notes-to-self:
- When debugging, always gather: pod imageID, node imageRef, registry manifest digests for tag, registry-proxy cache headers.
- Keep a short script to produce cross-node digest matrix (I'll write it and drop here later).

End of scratchpad.

-- Aisha
